questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code decides which accounts are allowed to authenticate? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
A caller posts /auth/login for an e-mail address that has no account, and another caller posts a wrong password for an existing active account. What can each caller observe?
choices: The first gets 404 invalid_user, the second gets 401 invalid_credentials
Both get 401 with the same body, because DaoAuthenticationProvider converts the missing-user case into a bad-credentials failure
Both get 500, because UsernameNotFoundException is not handled by the controller
The first gets 401, the second gets 403 because the account exists

questions.prompt: An old account was stored with a hash whose prefix is not the delegating encoder's default, for example `{pbkdf2@SpringSecurity_v5_8}...`. The user logs in with the right password. What happens beyond the successful login?
choices: Nothing; the stored hash is never changed by a login
The login fails because only the default encoding is accepted
The hash is verified with the matching legacy encoder, then re-encoded with the current default and saved through `updatePassword`
The controller's register path is invoked to create a new account with the new encoding

questions.prompt: A developer adds `GET /internal/reports` in a new controller and changes nothing in SecurityConfig. Who can call it?
choices: Anyone, since only the listed paths have explicit rules
Only requests with a valid session cookie, because sessions are the default
Only requests carrying a CSRF token, since CSRF protection protects new endpoints
Only requests that present a valid bearer JWT, because the chain ends with `anyRequest().authenticated()`
